  - Lists the series' released games with Japan, North America and PAL release dates and a notes block each
  - Adds three games the series page does not list: Chocobo World (PocketStation minigame of Final Fantasy VIII, 1999-02-11 in Japan; included in the Windows version of Final Fantasy VIII, 2000), Chocobo Stallion and Dice de Chocobo (both 1999-12-22, in the Chocobo Collection compilation)
  - Chocobo Collection (1999-12-22) compiles Chocobo Racing, Chocobo Stallion and Dice de Chocobo; Dice de Chocobo was released on Game Boy Advance in 2002 as Chocobo Land: A Game of Dice
  - Chocobo's Mysterious Dungeon notes: released on PlayStation (1997-12-23, Japan only), also available on WonderSwan (1999) and PlayStation Network (2010); Chocobo's Dungeon 2 notes: PlayStation, also on PlayStation Network (2010), a WonderSwan Color version planned and not released
  - Dice de Chocobo notes: developed by Denyusha and published by Square in the Chocobo Collection; a board game; the PlayStation version is on PlayStation Network (2008); the Game Boy Advance version (Chocobo Land: A Game of Dice, 2002) came to the Nintendo Wii U Virtual Console on 2016-02-10
  - Chocobo Stallion notes: developed by ParityBit and published by Square in the Chocobo Collection; a Chocobo raising and racing simulation; also available on PlayStation Network (2008)
  - Chocobo Anywhere 2.5 is a stand-alone download of 2004, no day given; Chocobo Land: A Game of Dice is given as 2002, no day
  - Chocobo's Chocotto Farm (Chocobo no Chocotto Nouen, 2012-12-19): a farming game on the GREE mobile platform, developed by Smile-Lab, published by Square Enix
  - Removed or shut down per its notes: Chocobo Panic (removed from the Apple App Store in 2017), Chocobo's Crystal Tower ("later shut down"), Chocobo GP' ("later delisted from marketplaces")
  - Lists no article for: Chocobo GP', Chocobo no Chocotto Nouen, Chocobo's Crystal Tower, Chocobo Panic, Chocobo and the Magic Picture Book: The Witch, the Girl, and the Five Heroes, Chocobo de Mobile, Dokodemo Chocobo 1 to 3, Choco-Mate, Hataraku Chocobo, Chocobo Collection, Dice de Chocobo, Chocobo Stallion (user, 2026-10-23); the series page links articles for some of these

- https://finalfantasywiki.com/wiki/Chocobo_Collection -- Chocobo Collection is a compilation of three games (text pasted by user) -- accessed 2026-10-23; archived: TODO
  - A PlayStation compilation by Square, released only in Japan on 1999-12-22, the tenth anniversary of the chocobo's first appearance in Final Fantasy II; single player and multiplayer
  - Contains Chocobo Racing (a Mario Kart-style racing game, also released standalone in Japan and overseas), Chocobo Stallion (a breeding and racing game based on the Final Fantasy VII system) and Dice de Chocobo (a board game)
  - Left out of `contents[]`: Chocobo Collection (1999-12-22, PlayStation, Japan only) is an omnibus release of the three games above, like the other PlayStation omnibus releases of Final Fantasy titles, not a game of its own (user's call, 2026-10-23); its three games are parts, with the PlayStation row and the Collection's date where it is the earliest release

  - (fetched by me, text pasted by user; Tokyo Otaku Mode's Otapedia, sections Gameplay, Plot, Characters, Development, Reception)
  - a page on one game of the series, Chocobo Mystery Dungeon
  - The game: an RPG for the Nintendo Wii, Japan 2007 and the rest of the world 2008, remastered on the Nintendo DS in 2008
    - a related sequel, Chocobo's Mystery Dungeon: Every Buddy!, came to the Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 4 in 2019
    - random dungeons, a job system with ten jobs, card duels, WiFi battles
  - Plot (short): during a quest for the Timeless Power Gem, Cid and Chocobo fall into a vortex and land in Lostime on the island of Memoria, where a Bell of Oblivion makes everyone lose their memory
    - with Shirma and the mysterious Raffaello, Chocobo sets out to recover the residents' memories
    - this one game is not an entry of its own here
  - Series: it describes the Chocobo series as games that all feature the Chocobo, ranging from racing to card-based combat, with mixed to positive reviews and moderate success, sales dropping off quickly
    - consistent with the entry's description (casual fun around a recurring cast, different genres)
  - Its Links section names only https://www.square-enix.com/
- https://otakumode.com/otapedia/games/final_fantasy/chocobo_racing -- series, platforms, dates -- accessed 2026-10-17
  - (fetched by me, text pasted by user; Tokyo Otaku Mode's Otapedia, sections Gameplay, Characters, Plot)
  - a page on one game of the series, Chocobo Racing
  - The game: a kart-style racing game by Square for the Sony PlayStation in 1999, compared to Mario Kart and Crash Team Racing, starring Chocobo with Mog the Moogle and the Black Mage
    - modes: Story Mode (Cid narrates in a storybook style), Versus (multiplayer or against the computer), Grand-Prix, a relay race and Time Attack
    - Magic Stones (Haste, Fire, Blizzard, Thunder, Minimize, Reflect, Doom) that level up when collected again
    - average reviews
  - Plot (short): in chapters, Chocobo races challengers to uncover the mystery behind the blue crystals (Magicite shards of a crystal that the founder of Mysidia broke into eight pieces), travelling with the Moogle Mog
    - the White Mage tells them the secret if they beat her in a race
    - after all eight shards are gathered Bahamut opens a portal to the Esper kingdom of Fantasia after a race
    - the ending is a spoiler
    - this game is not an entry of its own here
  - Its Links section names only https://www.square-enix.com/

## dmkt-sp.jp (d game; Information)

- https://web.archive.org/web/20171017202521/https://www.dmkt-sp.jp/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fportal.dmkt-sp.jp%2Fsp%2Fgame-store%2Ftop -- Chocobo's Chocotto Farm (チョコボのチョコッと農園), listed on NTT Docomo's d game store, capture of 2017-10-17 -- accessed 2026-10-22; found by the user while checking the d game cloud service's store page; archived: TODO
  - The listing reads (translated): "A farm game full of cute animals. A farm game, the first social farm game from Square Enix, in which Chocobo, familiar from the Final Fantasy series, also appears"
  - The same listing is in the capture of 2016-10-12: https://web.archive.org/web/20161012012854/https://www.dmkt-sp.jp/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fportal.dmkt-sp.jp%2Fsp%2Fgame-store%2Ftop
  - d game was Docomo's portal for Android and iPhone social games (Game Watch, https://game.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/1470536.html, 2023-01-16); it ended 2023-09-27
  - The English title is a literal rendering of the Japanese (ちょこっと "just a little", 農園 "farm"); no official English title found; machine translation gives "Chocobo's Choco and Farm"
  - Not the next listing on the same page, ちょこっとファーム (Chokotto Farm, another publisher's farm game)
  - Platforms: Wikipedia's media list puts the game on GREE on 2012-12-19; the Play Store description says the Android version followed a feature-phone version that 600,000 people played, and Smile-Lab started the iOS and Android versions on 2015-09-16 (games.app-liv.jp, above); quicksave (https://quicksave.live/game/22908) lists iOS and Android on 2012-12-20; the capture does not say which devices each listed game ran on; d game was Docomo's portal for Android smartphones and iPhones, and the listing is on its smartphone store page (`sp/game-store`), which ended 2023-09-27 (an earlier end for the game itself is not known)
  - Unknown: publisher page, end date, and whether it also ran outside GREE and d game

## Decisions

- Chocobo Anywhere, 2, 2.5 and 3 stay four separate parts, not one rolled-up part with a date range: each has its own title, release year and phone models, and 2.5 is a download-only sequel. The two halves (前編 and 後編) of 2 and of 3 are one title each, not listed separately.
- Part order in Narrative and Chronological: array order (no sort keys); a sequel sits directly after the game it follows (and Chocobo GP, with the promotional Chocobo GP' after it, sits directly after Chocobo Racing): Chocobo's Dungeon 2 after Chocobo's Mysterious Dungeon, Final Fantasy Fables: Chocobo's Dungeon (a loose sequel) after Chocobo's Dungeon 2, Chocobo Tales: The Witch, the Girl, and the Five Heroes after Final Fantasy Fables: Chocobo Tales.
- Part order, series and promos: the Chocobo Anywhere games stay together, starting at the first game (Choco-Mate after them); the promotional Chocobo GP' follows Chocobo GP, as other promo entries follow the game they promote (Final Fantasy XI ~Adventure Log~, the Kingdom Hearts promo minigames).
- Part order, the Chocobo Collection's games: Chocobo Stallion, Chocobo Racing (with Chocobo GP and Chocobo GP' beside it), Dice de Chocobo, in the order Square Enix's page and the jacket obi list them, over the alphabetical order of the wikis; no official order exists beyond that listing.
- Chocobo's Chocotto Farm lists only the Chocobo-branded game: the renamed チョコッと農園, which has no Chocobo or Square Enix credit on the pages from 2018-10, is not Final Fantasy themed and is not listed on any portal (user's call).
- Chocobo World stays a part here and is also its own entry in group VIII (a minigame spin-off belongs with Final Fantasy VIII; the Chocobo series part is a shortcut row to it, linked by its anchor).
